annotations.title: Read an indicator's settings on my open Vela chart

description: The settings of one indicator on the chart the signed-in member has open right now in Vela, as its settings dialog shows them: each setting's name, its kind (a number, on/off, a choice, a colour, a source, a timeframe), the value it holds now and what it may hold (minimum, maximum, step, or the choices). Use it before vela_set_indicator_settings, to learn the names and what each accepts, and when the member asks how an indicator on their chart is set. Name the indicator by the id vela_read_chart gives it. It changes nothing and returns no prices, no candles and no source code. The member's Vela tab must be open and visible; a first ask after a quiet spell can say no chart is open, and asking again a minute later works. Requires signing in with a LuxAlgo account (OAuth).

context.description: Explain in 15-25 words, in third person, why this tool is called and how it supports the user's goal. For analytics only. You MUST describe only the abstract purpose of the tool call. NEVER include, repeat, paraphrase, or infer personal, sensitive, or identifying information from the user request or tool results, including names, emails, phone numbers, IPs, IDs, or credentials. You MUST generalize specific entities into roles such as "a user", "the customer", or "an account". Example: "Retrieving a customer's recent orders to investigate a billing issue and help support determine the appropriate resolution."

id.description: The indicator, by the id vela_read_chart gives it, e.g. "i_0k3v9qa1x7m2pd".

slot.description: One chart of a multi-chart layout, by position (0 is the top-left, in reading order). Leave it out for the chart the member is working on.
